## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs fixing before merge. It stores keys without lower-casing them, but `get` always looks keys up in lower case, so any value stored under a mixed-case key can never be read back. The added round-trip test only stores a lower-case key, so it passes despite this defect. The `DEFAULT_TTL` change and its updated comment are consistent with each other.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` (or `c.get("alpha")`) returns `None`, because `set` writes `self._store[key]` with the original casing while `get` reads `self._store.get(key.lower())` at app/cache.py:17. This breaks the rule in the comment at app/cache.py:14-15: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together". `test_set_then_get_round_trip` (tests/test_cache.py:10-14) only calls `set("alpha", ...)`, so it cannot catch this. Store under `key.lower()` in `set`, and add a test that calls `set` with a mixed-case key and reads it back with a different casing. — Callers moving from direct `_store` access to `set` with any mixed-case key always get a cache miss, and nothing signals an error. Their mixed-case entries also pile up in `_store` because `get` never finds them to evict them.

- `test_entries_expire` patches `time.monotonic` with a fixed clock, so the expiry check is deterministic and does not depend on real sleeps.
